title: The Afternoon Brief: Reese's Record Night, Carse Under Investigation, Yamashita Ties LPGA Mark
dek: Angel Reese shattered two WNBA rebounding records in a single game Monday as Atlanta topped Los Angeles, while England's cricket discipline crisis deepened with Brydon Carse removed from the Pakistan squad and the Cricket Regulator opening a formal investigation. Across sports, a study documented CTE in 215 of 235 deceased NFL players, Sir Billy Boston died at 92, and the Astros parted ways with general manager Dana Brown amid unconfirmed details.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Reese's dual record-breaking performance marks a historic offensive surge for a Dream team eyeing the playoffs, while England's third disciplinary benching this summer signals an institutional pattern the captain has already flagged as problematic.
bottom_line: Today's thread connects record-breaking performances with disciplinary crisis and high-profile transitions across sports. Reese's dual WNBA records and Yamashita's LPGA benchmark marked historic individual achievements, while England's third disciplinary benching in a summer and a new CTE study extending the safety conversation beyond the professional level signaled systemic questions in their respective sports. The honest read is that several developments, Carse's investigation, the Astros separation, the WNBA eligibility tension, remain unsettled, with key facts or official statements still pending. Watch for the Cricket Regulator's findings on Carse, confirmation of the Astros' front-office succession, and whether Atlanta's rebounding surge carries into the playoffs.
body: Angel Reese recorded 26 rebounds in Atlanta's 78-71 win over Los Angeles on Monday, breaking the WNBA single-game record of 24 set by Chamique Holdsclaw in 2003 and pushing her season total to 458 boards, surpassing A'ja Wilson's single-season mark. The performance came during a four-game stretch in which Reese has produced at historically high offensive and rebounding levels, including a career-high 31 points against Phoenix on Saturday and a perfect 9-of-9 shooting night with 20 points and 10 rebounds against Las Vegas. Her 11 points, three assists, and three steals on Monday marked her 27th double-double of the season.

In cricket, England's disciplinary crisis deepened as the Cricket Regulator opened a formal investigation into fast bowler Brydon Carse following his removal from the Pakistan Test squad. Carse, who has taken 58 wickets since his Test debut in October 2024 more than any other England bowler in that span, was filmed in handcuffs outside a Derby bar on August 22 or August 23 (accounts in available reporting differ on the exact date). He was de-arrested after agreeing to leave the area and released without charge. Carse becomes the third England player benched this summer for a disciplinary breach, a pattern that prompted captain Ben Root to call for improved behavior. Sonny Baker, 23, has been named his replacement.

A study published in the British Medical Journal documented chronic traumatic encephalopathy in 215 of 235 deceased former NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 and donated their brains to research. Researchers attributed cumulative head impacts across youth, high school, and college levels, not just professional play, as the primary driver of the disease's prevalence. On a lighter note, Miyu Yamashita tied the LPGA's 72-hole scoring record at 23-under 257 at the CPKC Women's Open in Canada, winning by nine shots with a dominant final round that included six birdies. The 25-year-old Japanese player claimed her fourth LPGA victory in 13 months.

Sir Billy Boston, rugby league's first knighted player and a pioneer as the first black British player to tour Australia and New Zealand in 1954, died at 92. Boston scored 571 tries in his career, second only to Brian Bevan, and received his knighthood from King Charles in 2025 weeks before his death. Elsewhere, a courtside confrontation between former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom and Chicago Sky guard Natasha Cloud during a timeout at Sunday's Sky-Fever game resulted in Kanter Freedom's ejection. He was wearing a shirt reading "WOMAN noun. Adult human female." The incident centers on the WNBA's transgender eligibility rule. Finally, the Astros and general manager Dana Brown are reported to have parted ways, though the circumstances, timing, and succession details remain unconfirmed pending an official statement from the club or Major League Baseball.
